newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania miners' union protests over Cosma arrest.
newsitem.headline: Romania miners' union protests over Cosma arrest.

text.p: Leaders of Romania's Jiu Valley coalminers protested on Saturday against the detention of their union chief, Miron Cosma, the man accused of spearheading bloody riots in early post-communist years

Romania's new centrist government has pledged to bring to justice those responsible for violence in 1991 when Cosma's miners beat up protesters and ransacked party offices to silence opposition to old guard leaders around then president Ion Iliescu.

Police detained Cosma on Friday on a warrant accusing him of "undermining state authority" and breaking firearms regulations, charges which carry up to 15 years jail. No date for his trial has been set.
State news agency Rompres said miners' union leaders met in their Petrosani on Saturday and issued a statement declining "responsibility for any unrest" that might result from the arrest.
Police said Petrosani, the main Jiu Valley mining town, 350 km (218 miles) west of Bucharest, was calm.
Centrist president Emil Constantinescu accepted a request from Jiu Valley miners leaders to meet him at his Cotroceni palace on Sunday, a presidential official said.
Cosma led thousands of Jiu Valley coalminers to Bucharest for a three-day rampage in 1991. Government offices were torched and three people were killed during clashes with security forces.

Former Prime Minister Petre Roman, a reformer who led Romania's first post-communist government until he was toppled by the miners' riots, hailed Cosma's arrest, saying it was "high time for justice have its say."
Now head of the Senate, Roman regards his downfall as a putsch engineered by communists around Iliescu.

Iliescu called Cosma's arrest an "exaggerated move", saying that the 1991 riots had been "spontaneous." He has repeatedly denied accusations of resorting to mob rule by summoning the miners to the capital to crush opposition protests.
Cosma's star has been on the wane in recent years. He failed to win a parliament seat in elections last November which also removed Iliescu's leftists from office for the first time in seven years.
